task.title: Apply caller-selected limits during atomic tool activation
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/629 by applying one caller-selected resource policy uniformly across an atomically activated tool batch.
acceptance_criteria: Expose an additive explicit-policy activation operation for one ToolExecutionLimits value.
Keep default activation API-compatible by delegating with default limits.
Preserve atomic registration, exact-ID ordering, revalidation, inert construction, and empty no-op behavior.
Apply restrictive limits only after authorization when invocation creates a fresh store.

attempts.summary: Established RED coverage for explicit activation policy.
attempts.diagnostic: Atomic activation always used built-in defaults and exposed no activate_tool_selection_with_limits operation.
attempts.patch: Added integration tests requiring explicit restrictive limits and an empty explicit-policy activation after removing the root.

attempts.diagnostic: Constructing every inert adapter with one copied policy keeps batch semantics simple while allowing callers to tighten limits without bypassing atomic activation.
attempts.patch: Added activate_tool_selection_with_limits and made default activation delegate with ToolExecutionLimits::default.

attempts.summary: Verified limits remain inert until authorized invocation.
attempts.diagnostic: A restrictive instance limit must not execute or reject a valid component during activation, but must fail when a later authorized invocation instantiates it.
attempts.patch: Covered successful registration followed by resource-limited invocation failure and documented the uniform policy boundary.

outcome.summary: Callers can now apply one explicit resource policy uniformly during atomic activation while default behavior remains compatible and guest execution remains authorization-gated.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo test --locked -p vela-extensions --test activation
GitHub Rust quality gate https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/actions/runs/30214708288 and substantive exact-head CodeRabbit review at https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/pull/630

lessons: Caller-selected policy should remain available at the highest safe atomic activation boundary.
One uniform batch policy avoids premature per-tool manifest configuration and reusable grants.
Restrictive execution policy belongs to fresh invocation stores, not inert compilation or registration.
API compatibility is simplest when the default operation delegates to the explicit-policy operation.
